title: Stream choke: circuit-breaker hotfix for multi-length request latency spikes
creator: Ethan Brooks
description: Multiple enterprise customers (Acme Analytics and Nimbus Health) reported sustained increases in first-token latency and severe drop in token/sec for mixed short/long request workloads across Hosted, Dedicated and Private deployments. Symptoms include stalled streaming responses (long pauses between initial token and subsequent tokens), elevated TTFT for short prompts (<=32 tokens), and throughput collapse for short-burst workloads. This ticket tracks root cause, mitigation, and a rapid hotfix deploy sequence.
observed_metrics_and_windows: Baseline median TTFT (short requests) ~120ms; observed median TTFT 420–670ms during incidents
95th-percentile TTFT spiked from 340ms to 1.2s in US-West clusters
Tokens/sec for affected model-family dropped from ~1800 tok/s to ~400–700 tok/s during bursts
Spike correlated with mixed prompt distribution (20% short <=32 tokens + 80% long >1k tokens) and kernel-picker v2.4 rollout
Incidents began 2026-03-09 06:30 UTC, recurring waves through 2026-03-11 with customer escalations
reproduction_steps: Deploy kernel-picker v2.4 on a staging runtime with multiplex enabled
Simulate mixed workload: 20% short synchronous streaming requests (<=32 tokens) and 80% long generation requests (>1000 tokens) across a 10-node pool
Observe scheduler prefetch and KV cache thrash traces; confirm long pauses between tokens for short requests
Run perf harness 'mixbench-v2' with tags model-family=redwood-open-xxlarge to reproduce tokens/sec drop
root_cause_summary: Kernel-selection heuristic (kernel-picker v2.4) misclassifies request shape in multiplex pools with mixed request lengths, causing aggressive prefetching and oversized microbatch scheduling for worker lanes that then stall short-streamed requests. This interacts with recent continuous-batching changes that assume homogeneous context windows, resulting in KV-cache eviction churn and scheduler head-of-line blocking for low-latency streams.
mitigation_actions_taken: Backed out kernel-picker v2.4 flag in hosted us-west-2 (rolling rollback completed 2026-03-11 03:40 UTC) to restore previous stable heuristic
Deployed temporary per-tenant short-request hedging: duplicate-first-token requests for short streams to a low-latency lane (hedge window 50ms)
Introduced a prefetch budget limiter (prefetch_budget=0.2) to avoid oversubscribing worker KV cache during mixed workloads
Pushed an emergency config patch to Dedicated clusters and shipped an advisory + patch bundle for Private customers (on-prem) with step-by-step rollback guidance
rollback_plan: If elevated TTFT persists after hotfix, perform immediate rollback: set kernel-picker flag to v2.3 in all active pools
Route affected tenants to low-latency lanes via routing policy 'short-first' until permanent fix is validated
Notify Dedicated customers via incident channel and schedule coordinated maintenance window for on-prem patching
rollout_plan: Stage 0: apply prefetch_budget limiter + hedging in a canary subset of Hosted us-west-2 (3 nodes) - 30 min observation
Stage 1: expand to all Hosted us-west-2 and us-east-1, target wait 60m monitoring window
Stage 2: apply config to Dedicated clusters with staged hosts (10% -> 50% -> 100%)
Stage 3: provide Private patch with automated installer (sha256 verified) and runbook for customer ops; coordinate with SRE and SE teams
acceptance_criteria: Median TTFT for short requests returns to baseline +/-15% in affected regions
Tokens/sec recovers to >85% of pre-incident baseline under mixed workload bench
No increase in error-rate or model output regressions observed in 24h post-rollout
Affected customer threads show reduced escalation severity (customers confirm acceptable latency)
qa_checks: Run 'mixbench-v2' with production seed for 3 hours on canary after hotfix
Smoke test streaming API across Hosted/Dedicated/Private with 50 simultaneous short streams
Run synthetic prober that alternates long/short requests to validate no head-of-line blocking
Confirm KV cache hit-rate does not drop by >10% post-change
communication_and_customer_notes: 2026-03-11 04:12 UTC: initial customer advisory sent to Acme Analytics and Nimbus Health (PM: Claire Jensen)
2026-03-11 05:00 UTC: follow-up with Dedicated customers including targeted mitigation steps and ETA for full fix
Provide Private customers a hotfix bundle and step-by-step installer; offer SRE-assisted apply within SLA window
postmortem_todo: Replace kernel-picker heuristic with model-aware estimator that accounts for context-length variance
Add long-short workload fuzz-tests to CI that specifically validate streaming latencies under multiplex
Improve telemetry: correlate per-tenant KV cache evictions with per-request TTFT and surface in console
Document operational runbook for mixed-workload mitigations (routing policies, prefetch tuning)
notes: Trade-offs: hedging reduces duplicate-work and slightly increases cost for short requests; prefetch limiter may slightly reduce long-request throughput in extreme cases
Engineering review (2026-03-12): decided temporary hedging + prefetch limiter is safest fast mitigation while engineering implements a model-aware kernel selector
SRE and SE alignment meeting scheduled 2026-03-13 14:00 UTC to co-ordinate Dedicated and Private rollouts
